newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks surge for 2nd session on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks surge for 2nd session on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks surged in strong trade for the second straight session as foreign investors continued their buying spree for liquid Venezuelan blue-chips, traders said.
"They see some life in the privatization program and labor reforms. From here on in we could enter a virtuous circle. The market looks strong," said Activalores broker Gonzalo Alonso.
Companies with American Depository Receipt (ADR) listings performed strongest, brokers said, with telephone company CANTV up over three percent, and foods company Mavesa up 4.3 percent.

The market's 19-share index rose 1.34 percent to close at 6,451.06 points. Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, meanwhile gained 1.74 percent to end at 101.26 points. The session's rise marked a regaining of ground lost over the first four months of 1997. Merinvest's index is re-based at 100.00 at the beginning of each year.

"Investors see a market that has stagnated for five months even as the economy has grown," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino, adding that prices could continue to rise as foreign bidders sought block buys in a supply-squeezed market.
"That could pressure prices further upwards," he said.
Trade volume was boosted to 137 million shares worth 4.4 billion bolivars ($9 million) -- the highest of the year -- as 115 million Corimon B issue shares exchanged hands.
Corimon B shares are company debts capitalized under a financial restructuring plan worked-out late last year for the struggling paints and packaging company.

"The vendor of the shares, which are worth some two percent of the company, was by a local financial institution for whom the stake did not hold any strategic interest," said one broker. The stock closed flat at 9.15 bolivars as among total traded issues 20 rose, seven fell and 10 closed flat.
